cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to Timothy, whom he calls his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:1-2). Paul's been walking him through how to treat people in the church, like the widows (1 Timothy 5:3-16). Now Paul turns to the elders who lead.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says elders who lead effectively are worthy of double honor.
Paul says some of those elders who lead well deserve that honor ESPECIALLY. Which ones?

answers.text: Those who work hard at preaching and teaching
Those who have served in the church the longest
Those who were the first ones chosen to lead

cards.text: Paul backs it up with Scripture, one line about an ox and one about getting paid. My pay for all those years in the junk drawer? DUST. Paid in full, friend.

cards.question: The Scripture Paul quotes says not to muzzle an ox while it's doing what?
Paul's second line from Scripture is about getting paid: “The worker is worthy of his ___.”
Someone brings an accusation against an elder. Paul tells Timothy not to entertain it except on the testimony of two or three ___.
Paul says those who persist in sin should be rebuked so that the others will stand in fear of sin. How should they be rebuked?

cards.text: Then Paul gets SERIOUS. He solemnly charges Timothy before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels, and friend, that is NOT a sticky note on the oven.

cards.question: True or false: Paul charges Timothy to keep these principles but go a little easier on the people he likes.
Paul has a warning for Timothy about the laying on of hands. True or false: he tells Timothy to be quick about it.

cards.text: Paul says rushing it means sharing in the sins of others, so keep yourself pure. Then Paul goes from the elect angels to checking on Timothy's health, and THAT'S a friend.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to stop drinking only water and use a little wine instead. Why?

answers.text: Because of his stomach and frequent ailments
Because the water in that city is unclean
Because he has a long journey ahead

cards.question: Back to sin. Paul says the sins of some men are obvious, going ahead of them to judgment. What about the sins of others?

answers.text: They are never found out at all

cards.question: Paul says good deeds work the same way. True or false: the good deeds nobody notices stay hidden forever.

cards.text: Even the quiet good deeds can't stay hidden. It's like that ONE cookie that rolls under the oven, friend. Somebody ALWAYS finds it.
Last stretch. Paul turns to all who are under the yoke of slavery, and how they should regard their masters.

cards.question: Paul says those under the yoke of slavery should regard their masters as fully worthy of honor. Why?

answers.text: So God's name and our teaching aren't discredited
So they can earn their freedom much sooner
So their masters will start treating them better

cards.question: Some of them have believing masters. Paul says they should not show disrespect just because those masters are ___.

cards.text: Instead, they should serve them all the more, since the ones getting that good service are beloved believers. And Paul hands Timothy his job: teach and encourage these principles.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "The worker is worthy of his ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Card 4 already says the second Scripture line is 'about getting paid,' and card 6's own question repeats it ('Paul's second line from Scripture is about getting paid'). That gives away 'wages' and rules out 'rest' and 'praise.'

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the quoted line 'The worker is worthy of his ___.' This tests the line's wording instead of its meaning or movement.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Cards 7 and 8 bring in new moments (accusations against an elder in 5:19, and rebuking those who persist in sin in 5:20) with no story card setting them up. Cards 5 through 8 are four choice cards in a row, and the new material is told only inside the questions.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card. Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

findings.problem: Card 12 says 'so keep yourself pure,' which makes keeping pure a result of not sharing in others' sins. The text gives 'Keep yourself pure' as a separate command and doesn't connect the two.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 12 says Paul is 'checking on Timothy's health' just before card 13 asks why Timothy should use a little wine. That gives away the health answer and rules out the water and journey answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 16 restates what card 15 just answered ('Even the quiet good deeds can't stay hidden') and adds only a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The joke could ride on card 17 or be folded into a setup card instead.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
